title: Fibre support bound for compactly supported higher direct images at finite coefficients
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring whose additive exponent is invertible in $k$. Use the ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated morphism of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $d\ge0$ be an integer such that every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$, $y\in Y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], has topological Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $Rf_!$ be the compact-support direct image of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and $R^qf_!=\mathcal H^qRf_!$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and $a\ge0$ an integer such that the closed support of a sheaf (the complement of the largest Zariski open on which it vanishes; by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] this is the closure of the set of points with a nonzero geometric stalk) $Z$ of $F$ has dimension at most $a$. Then for every integer $q$ the closed support of $R^qf_!F$ has dimension at most $a+d-q$, the empty set having dimension $-\infty$. In particular $R^qf_!F=0$ for $q<0$ and for $q>a+d$.

source.place: 4.2.4 (support estimate for the compact-support direct image along fibres of dimension <= d)

proof.text: Choose a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}Y$ by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Here $Y$ is qcqs, $f$ is separated of finite type, and $\overline X$ is finite type over $k$ since $r$ is proper. Use $Rf_!=Rr_*Dj_!$ as defined in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Apply [lem-fd-finite-ring-compact-support-finiteness] to $F[0]$ and this compactification. It gives constructibility of every $G_q=R^qf_!F$ and $G_q=0$ for $q<0$ (its amplitude clause with $[a,b]=[0,0]$). The sheaf $F[0]$ is bounded constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

source.place: 4.2.4: finite-coefficient sheaf support estimate, fibrewise argument

proof.text: For each $q$, [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-support-constructible] makes the nonzero-stalk set $S_q$ constructible and makes its definition independent of the geometric point over a fixed point. Its closure is the closed support $C_q$: an open set misses $S_q$ exactly when the restricted sheaf is zero by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. The schemes here are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. In particular [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] gives finitely many irreducible components of $C_q$.

source.place: 4.2.4: finite-coefficient sheaf support estimate, fibrewise argument

proof.text: The generic point $t$ of every irreducible component $T$ of $C_q$ belongs to $S_q$. Indeed, remove the other finitely many components and work on the resulting nonempty open subset of $T$. It meets $S_q$ densely. Express $S_q$ as a finite union of locally closed sets by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Some one of their closures is all of $T$: a finite closed cover of an irreducible space has a member equal to the space. This locally closed set therefore contains a nonempty open of $T$, and hence its generic point. Thus $t\in S_q$.

source.place: 4.2.4: finite-coefficient sheaf support estimate, fibrewise argument

proof.text:
Fix $y\in Y$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(y)$, giving $\bar y:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$; write $r':\overline X_{\bar y}\to P$, $j_{\bar y}$ and $F_{\bar y}$ for the base changes and $H=j_{\bar y!}F_{\bar y}$. Proper base change [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] for the proper map $r$, applied to $Dj_!F$, and [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] for $j$ (degreewise, on the single sheaf $j_!F$) give $\bar y^{-1}Rf_!F\cong Rr'_*H$ in $D(P_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Taking cohomology and stalks commutes by [lem-kun-stalks-of-cohomology]. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] a stalk at $\bar y$ is $\Gamma(P,\bar y^{-1}(-))$ and $\Gamma(P,-)$ is exact, so $(G_q)_{\bar y}\cong\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(P,Rr'_*H))$. Represent $Rr'_*H$ by $r'_*I$ for a K-injective resolution $H\to I$, as in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Termwise $\Gamma(P,r'_*I)=\Gamma(\overline X_{\bar y},I)$ by the direct-image formula recorded in [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], whose cohomology is $H^q(\overline X_{\bar y},H)$ by [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]; module and abelian cohomology agree by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget]. Therefore
$$(G_q)_{\bar y}\cong H^q(\overline X_{\bar y},j_{\bar y!}F_{\bar y}).$$
All coefficient sheaves are torsion because the additive exponent of $\Lambda$ kills them; proper base change allows this arbitrary geometric base change.

source.place: Proper base change (Tag 095T); geometric-point cohomology Tags 03QT/03QU; extension by zero and pullback

proof.text: Give $Z$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Put $Z_y=Z\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$. If it is nonempty, write $e(y)=\dim Z_y$. The closed immersion into $X_y$ gives $e(y)\le d$: chains of irreducible closed subsets stay chains in $X_y$. For the field extension $\kappa(y)\subset\Omega$, [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] preserves local fibre dimensions. The projection $Z_{\bar y}\to Z_y$ is surjective: above a point $z$ its fibre is the spectrum of the nonzero ring $\kappa(z)\otimes_{\kappa(y)}\Omega$, nonzero by a vector-space basis. Consequently $\dim Z_{\bar y}=\dim Z_y=e(y)$. To see the global dimension conclusion from the local one, use the finite irreducible components of these finite-type schemes, [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic] on each component, and the definition of local dimension [def-kun-dimension]: the maximum of component dimensions is both the global dimension and the maximum of the local dimensions. Empty fibres stay empty.

source.place: 4.2.4: finite-coefficient sheaf support estimate, fibrewise argument

proof.text: Let $W$ be the closure of $Z_{\bar y}$ in $\overline X_{\bar y}$, with reduced induced structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Since $Z_{\bar y}$ is closed in the open $X_{\bar y}$, it is locally closed, hence constructible. Apply [lem-per-constructible-subset-closure-dimension] over $\Omega$ to get $\dim W=e(y)$ when nonempty. The sheaf $H=j_{\bar y!}F_{\bar y}$ vanishes outside $W$: it is zero outside $X_{\bar y}$ by extension by zero and outside $Z_{\bar y}$ inside that open by the closed support of $F$ and conservativity of geometric stalks [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. By [lem-kun-04ca], its underlying abelian sheaf is $i_*i^{-1}H$, where $i:W\hookrightarrow\overline X_{\bar y}$ is the closed immersion. This also handles $W=\varnothing$, giving $H=0$.

source.place: 4.2.4: finite-coefficient sheaf support estimate, fibrewise argument

proof.text:
For $W\ne\varnothing$, the closed immersion $i$ is finite: on affine charts its map is $A\to A/I$, generated by $1$ as an $A$-module. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology] gives
$$H^q(\overline X_{\bar y},H)\cong H^q(W,i^{-1}H)\quad(q\ge0)$$
for underlying abelian sheaves. Module cohomology has the same underlying groups by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget]. The field $\Omega$ is separably closed, so [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(\Omega)\le0$; apply [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] to the finite-type $\Omega$-scheme $W$ of dimension $e(y)$ and the torsion sheaf $i^{-1}H$. Combining with Steps 4--6, the stalk of $G_q$ is zero if $Z_y$ is empty or $q>2e(y)$.

source.place: 4.2.4: finite-coefficient sheaf support estimate, fibrewise argument

proof.text: Take $q\ge0$ and an irreducible component $T$ of the nonempty closed support $C_q$, with generic point $t$. By Step 3 the stalk there is nonzero. Step 7 implies $Z_t\ne\varnothing$ and $q\le2e(t)\le2d$. Choose an irreducible component $B$ of $Z_t$ of dimension $e(t)$ and let $Z'$ be its closure in $Z$, with reduced induced structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Then $Z'$ is an irreducible finite-type $k$-scheme, $\overline{f(Z')}=T$, and its fibre over $t$ has underlying space $B$. For the last assertion, $Z'\subseteq f^{-1}(T)$ since that is closed and contains $B$. The fibre over the generic point $t$ embeds topologically into $f^{-1}(t)$ by affine localization (the description of [def-pc-scheme-fibre]); intersecting the closure of $B$ with that fibre gives its closure in the fibre, which is $B$ since $B$ is closed there. The generic point $\zeta$ of $Z'$ is the generic point of $B$ and lies over $t$.

source.place: 4.2.4: finite-coefficient sheaf support estimate, fibrewise argument

proof.text:
Apply [lem-zl-irreducible-fibre-dimension-lower-bound] to $Z'\to Y$: there is $r\ge0$ with $\dim Z'=\dim T+r$, and the locus where the local fibre dimension equals $r$ is dense open in $Z'$. This open contains its generic point $\zeta$. The fibre $Z'_t$ is irreducible finite type over $\kappa(t)$ with underlying space $B$; [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic] therefore says its local dimension at $\zeta$ equals its dimension $e(t)$. Hence $r=e(t)$ and
$$\dim T=\dim Z'-e(t)\le a-e(t)\le a-\lceil q/2\rceil.$$
Here $\dim Z'\le\dim Z\le a$ follows by including chains of closed irreducible subsets, and $e(t)\ge\lceil q/2\rceil$ follows from $q\le2e(t)$.

Since $q\le2d$, $\lfloor q/2\rfloor\le d$, so
$$\dim T\le a-\lceil q/2\rceil=a-q+\lfloor q/2\rfloor\le a+d-q.$$
The finitely many irreducible components $T$ cover $C_q$, so this bounds $\dim C_q$: the largest member of a chain of irreducible closed subsets in a finite closed cover lies in one cover member, by irreducibility, and then the whole chain does. If $a+d-q<0$, a nonempty component would have dimension at least zero; hence $C_q=\varnothing$, and geometric-stalk conservativity gives $G_q=0$ [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. For empty $C_q$ the asserted dimension bound uses $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$; negative $q$ were covered in Step 1.
